lessons.text: Finishing a change in this repo: write new .py files (test modules, any new package modules) with `# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0` as line 1 from the start; `ls`/`find` the tree first and check whether tests/ already has tests before adding any (it may, e.g. tests/test_tax.py); if you create tests/ yourself, add an empty tests/__init__.py — `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .` raises `ImportError: Start directory is not importable: 'tests'` without it; run the CI command exactly as CI does it — `APP_ENV=test python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .` (note `-t .`); add a bullet under `## Unreleased` in CHANGELOG.md (create it with `# Changelog` if absent); for bug fixes name a test `test_regression_*`; end the final report with a `Risk: low|medium|high` line — if CI flags only that line, re-state the same report with it instead of touching code.
lessons.evidence: This session had no tests/ at all and `APP_ENV=test python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .` failed with "ImportError: Start directory is not importable: 'tests'"; creating an empty tests/__init__.py (plus tests/test_ops.py) made the same command run 6 tests OK, and CI then reported "✓ tests". Omitting that step would have left the tests check red.

lessons.text: CI for this project has a mypy/pydocstyle check (not in the repo): every new public function needs full type annotations (all args and return) and/or a docstring — write both from the start, e.g. `def reverse_words(s: str) -> str:` plus a one-line docstring. Older functions like strings/ops.py's `shout` (no annotations, no docstring, no module docstring) are grandfathered and pydocstyle still reports D100/D103 on them locally, so only the new symbol matters. Locally verify with `python3 -m mypy --explicit-package-bases strings tests` (plain `mypy strings/ tests/` fails with a duplicate-module/explicit-package-base error that is not a code problem) and `python3 -m pydocstyle strings/ops.py`.
lessons.evidence: CI report flagged 'strings/ops.py: reverse_words: missing annotations (all args and return) or docstring' after I added the unannotated, undocumented function.

lessons.text: When you add a public function to code that is grandfathered without annotations or docstrings, still write full type annotations and a one-line docstring on the new function: match the file's naming/structure style, but CI checks the new symbol and fails it with "missing annotations (all args and return) or docstring".
lessons.evidence: I wrote `def reverse_words(s):` to match the bare style of `shout` in strings/ops.py; the CI report then failed with "mypy/pydocstyle: strings/ops.py: reverse_words: missing annotations (all args and return) or docstring", requiring a second turn to add `s: str -> str` and a docstring.

lessons.text: This repo's CI has an `error-policy` check (not in the repo) that passes when library code raises the package's own exception base (e.g. users/errors.py AppError) instead of a builtin like ValueError; raising AppError for bad input satisfied it.
lessons.evidence: The CI report for the validate_age change (raising users.errors.AppError for negative ages) came back all green including `✓ error-policy`, confirming raising the package's AppError over a builtin is the accepted policy.

lessons.text: pydocstyle (CI's mypy/pydocstyle check) also reports D100 on the module you touch: when you edit an existing module that has no module docstring (like users/validate.py, which is otherwise grandfathered), add a one-line module docstring in the same pass, then confirm with `python3 -m pydocstyle <file>`.
lessons.evidence: After editing users/validate.py (a grandfathered file with no module docstring), `python3 -m pydocstyle users/validate.py` failed with "users/validate.py:1 at module level: D100: Missing docstring in public module"; adding a one-line module docstring ("\"\"\"Validation helpers for user attributes.\"\"\"") made it clean. Lesson #8 says only the new symbol matters for CI, so without this the local pydocstyle run stays dirty on every file I edit and I have to spend a second pass to clear it.

lessons.text: Finishing a change in this repo: write new .py files (test modules, any new package modules) with `# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0` as line 1 from the start; `ls`/`find` the tree first and check whether tests/ already has tests before adding any (it may, e.g. tests/test_tax.py); if you create tests/ yourself, add an empty tests/__init__.py — `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .` raises `ImportError: Start directory is not importable: 'tests'` without it; run the CI command exactly as CI does it — `APP_ENV=test python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .` (note `-t .`); add a bullet under `## Unreleased` in CHANGELOG.md (create it with `# Changelog` if absent); for bug fixes name a test `test_regression_*`; end the final report with a `Risk: low|medium|high` line — if CI flags only that line, re-state the same report with it instead of touching code.
lessons.evidence: This session had no tests/ at all and `APP_ENV=test python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .` failed with "ImportError: Start directory is not importable: 'tests'"; creating an empty tests/__init__.py (plus tests/test_ops.py) made the same command run 6 tests OK, and CI then reported "✓ tests". Omitting that step would have left the tests check red.

lessons.text: This repo has no CHANGELOG.md until you create one: make it with a `# Changelog` heading and a `## Unreleased` section holding the bullet, which satisfies the CI changelog check.
lessons.evidence: `ls -a` at the start and `cat CHANGELOG.md` showed no changelog file; I wrote one with `# Changelog` + `## Unreleased` + a "- Fixed `Stock.remove` ..." bullet, and the following CI report listed only "✓ tests / ✗ regression-tests" with no changelog complaint.

lessons.text: CI for this project has a `license-header` check: every new .py file must start with `# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0` on line 1 (older files like shapes/square.py are grandfathered and lack it).
lessons.evidence: CI report failed with "license-header: shapes/circle.py:1: missing `# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0`"; adding the header as the first line of shapes/circle.py fixed it.

lessons.text: This repo's package layout and tests/ contents differ between sessions (shapes/, loader/, and this session billing/ + tests/test_tax.py), so `ls`/`find` the tree at the start, don't assume any particular package, and don't assume the CI `tests` check is vacuous — tests may already exist.
lessons.evidence: Old lesson #4 claimed "This repo has no tests/ directory at the start of a session, so the CI tests check passes vacuously"; this session `ls -la` showed billing/, tests/ (with __init__.py and test_tax.py) already present, so that claim was stale and the vacuous-pass reasoning would have been wrong.

lessons.text: This repo's CI has a lint rule L001 (not in the repo): library code must not use print or warnings.warn — it needs a module logger (`logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)`) and `logger.warning(...)` instead.
lessons.evidence: CI report on the missing-config-file change failed with "lint: loader/config.py: library code must not print/warnings.warn (L001: module logger required)" after I implemented the warning with warnings.warn; switching to a module logger and assertLogs made it pass.

lessons.text: This environment runs Python 3.11.6 (`python3`), so 3.10+ APIs such as `self.assertNoLogs` are available.
lessons.evidence: I ran `python3 --version` before choosing assertLogs/assertNoLogs for the logging tests, getting "Python 3.11.6"; assertNoLogs needs 3.10+, so this decided the test style.

lessons.text: CI for this project has a `release-bot` check (not in the repo): the final report of the turn must end with a line of the form `Risk: low`, `Risk: medium` or `Risk: high`. Without it CI fails with "final report has no `Risk: low|medium|high` line at the end".
lessons.evidence: CI report for the greet() change said: "✗ release-bot: final report has no `Risk: low|medium|high` line at the end".

lessons.text: CI for this project has a mypy/pydocstyle check (not in the repo): every new public function needs full type annotations (all args and return) and/or a docstring — write both from the start, e.g. `def reverse_words(s: str) -> str:` plus a one-line docstring. Older functions like strings/ops.py's `shout` (no annotations, no docstring, no module docstring) are grandfathered and pydocstyle still reports D100/D103 on them locally, so only the new symbol matters. Locally verify with `python3 -m mypy --explicit-package-bases strings tests` (plain `mypy strings/ tests/` fails with a duplicate-module/explicit-package-base error that is not a code problem) and `python3 -m pydocstyle strings/ops.py`.
lessons.evidence: CI report flagged 'strings/ops.py: reverse_words: missing annotations (all args and return) or docstring' after I added the unannotated, undocumented function.

lessons.text: When you add a public function to code that is grandfathered without annotations or docstrings, still write full type annotations and a one-line docstring on the new function: match the file's naming/structure style, but CI checks the new symbol and fails it with "missing annotations (all args and return) or docstring".
lessons.evidence: I wrote `def reverse_words(s):` to match the bare style of `shout` in strings/ops.py; the CI report then failed with "mypy/pydocstyle: strings/ops.py: reverse_words: missing annotations (all args and return) or docstring", requiring a second turn to add `s: str -> str` and a docstring.
